saints.name: Sts. Francisco and Jacinta Marto
saints.title: Shepherd Children of Fátima
saints.shortBlurb: The two young shepherds of Fátima who saw the Virgin Mary and gave their short lives to prayer and penance for sinners…
biography: Francisco and Jacinta Marto, brother and sister of a shepherding family of Aljustrel near Fatima in Portugal, were eight and seven years old when, with their cousin Lucia dos Santos, they saw the Lady at the Cova da Iria on 13 May 1917, the first of six apparitions that year, following three visions of an angel in 1916.

Asked to pray the Rosary daily and to offer sacrifices for the conversion of sinners, the children gave themselves to prayer and penance with a single-mindedness that astonished their elders; Jacinta, moved by the vision of hell, longed to save souls, while Francisco loved to pray alone to console God.

In the influenza epidemic of 1918 both fell ill, and both accepted their sufferings as the Lady had foretold. Francisco died at home on 4 April 1919, aged ten; Jacinta died alone in a Lisbon hospital on 20 February 1920, aged nine, after an operation that removed two of her ribs.

Beatified by Pope John Paul II on 13 May 2000, they were canonized by Pope Francis at Fatima on 13 May 2017, the centenary of the first apparition, and remain the youngest children ever canonized who did not die as martyrs.
saints.knownFor: The visions of Fátima and their childlike life of prayer and penance.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of Sts. Francisco and Jacinta Marto (vatican.va)
